resources.string: To open Notification Inbox, swipe down on empty home-screen space, then slide back up toward where you started without lifting your finger. Release to open.
App guide
Navigation
Notification Inbox
Common tasks
Open your inbox

Enable notification access for Comfer in Android settings. Tap anywhere in the home notification row to open “%1$s”. You can also swipe down on empty home-screen space, slide back up toward where you started without lifting, and release to open the inbox. App icons show which apps have notifications; they are not separate buttons. When nothing is visible, an inbox icon keeps the entry available.
The three bottom tabs

“%1$s” (inbox icon): returns to current, visible notifications across apps and exits selection or configuration.

Saved (archive): shows locally saved notifications with a search input, only after they leave the active notification list. A notification never appears in both lists. Uses the same grouped or chronological view as “%1$s”. Tap a long preview to expand it, then tap again to open its app (the original notification destination is not retained). Long press to select, tap more copies or a group title to select them, and use “%2$s” at the bottom. For one selected copy, “%3$s” offers the same app protection and Android notification settings controls as “%1$s”. App protection also removes that app’s saved copies and stops its “%4$s” capture. “%5$s” opens a draft using its app/profile and saved title or message. Edit the suggested phrase and preview it against the saved reference; rules start in test-only mode. Multiple deletion requires confirmation. Back or “%6$s” exits selection. Swipe a copy to delete only that local copy. Copies whose preview is empty or hidden by Android are not saved. Enable capture under “%7$s” → “%4$s”.

Settings (gear): opens a directory for “%8$s”, “%9$s”, “%4$s” and “%10$s”. “%8$s” contains separate “%11$s” and “%12$s” pages. “%13$s” returns to the parent page. The gear returns to the settings directory from a child page.
Read, select and navigate

Notification bodies initially show one line. If more text is available, the first tap expands the full body and the next tap opens its destination in the source app. A single-line notification opens on the first tap. After a successful open, Comfer requests dismissal of eligible notifications. With “%1$s” enabled, an eligible copy is saved first and becomes available in “%2$s” after the notification leaves “%3$s”. Failed opens leave the notification active. Long press to enter selection mode and select that notification. Small selection circles become visible in their reserved space in front of every card; selected circles become filled circles. Text stays aligned when selection starts or ends. In selection mode, tap notifications or selection circles to select or deselect them.

Swipe a notification left or right to dismiss it when allowed; the card slides fully off-screen before removal. Protected or ongoing notifications cannot be dismissed through Comfer.

App groups show the app name and an up or down caret. Tap the caret to collapse or expand its notifications. In selection mode, tap the app name to select every notification in that group, including collapsed ones; tap it again when all are selected to deselect the group. Other groups keep their selections. “%4$s” view shows a flat list with newest items first. Scroll upward to use the full screen. Use “%5$s” to close “%6$s”, leave selection or return from “%7$s”. Returning from Android notification settings brings the selected notification back into view.
Actions on a notification

Long press a notification for the bottom quick menu.

Snooze: asks Android to bring selected notifications back in 15 minutes. Shown on Android 8 or newer only when every selected item is eligible.

Priority: places the selected apps first in grouped view. If all are already prioritized, it removes their priority; otherwise it prioritizes all of them. Android alert priority does not change.

More actions: available for a single selected notification and opens app controls. With multiple selections, only shared actions are shown. “%1$s” appears for multiple selections and clears them. Deselecting the last item exits selection automatically; “%2$s” also exits selection.
Dismiss, snooze and batch selection

Swipe a notification left or right to ask Android to dismiss it immediately. This removes the source notification; there is no swipe confirmation. Protected and ongoing notifications remain.

To dismiss several items, long press one and tap other notifications or selection circles. “%1$s” appears only when every selected notification is eligible. Tap it, then “%2$s”. If an item changes or disappears before execution, it may be skipped; a message appears if an action could not be completed.

Snooze in the quick menu postpones eligible selected notifications for 15 minutes. “%3$s” requires Android 8 or newer. Use “%4$s” or “%5$s” to leave selection without performing an action.
More actions: app controls

“%1$s” blocks Comfer’s dismissal and snooze actions for the app. “%2$s” restores eligible actions. Android may still protect ongoing notifications.\n\nSound and notification settings opens Android’s controls for the notification category or app. Use those controls to change sounds or disable alerts. For another profile, open the app’s settings inside that profile.
Inbox configuration

Notification view offers “%1$s” and “%2$s” side by side. The highlighted choice is active. “%1$s” puts priority apps first; “%2$s” shows the newest notifications first.

Below the view choices in Notification settings, “%3$s” / “%4$s” controls Comfer’s scheduled behavior and device quiet requests. “%5$s” also supports content rules: choose app/channel, title/message fields, required and exception phrases, preview, and save. Rules start in test-only mode. Disable “%6$s” to act; auto-dismiss requires separate confirmation and affects future events only. Regex is deferred.

Last successful refresh shows when the inbox last synced. “%7$s” retries synchronization. “%8$s” opens Android’s Do Not Disturb controls.

Reset notification settings requires confirmation, clears Comfer’s notification preferences and leaves automation paused. It does not dismiss your source notifications.
Focus timers and recurring quiet hours

Device quiet uses Android Do Not Disturb and requires separate Do Not Disturb access. The access button appears only while permission is missing. Android priority exceptions still apply.

Focus 15, 30 or 60 min starts a temporary quiet period. The timer shows its end time. “%1$s” appears while a timer is set and ends Comfer’s timer; an active schedule or other Android rules can still keep the device quiet. Restarting the phone ends a manual timer.

On Android 12 or newer, use “%2$s” in “%3$s” or a device-quiet recurring schedule to grant Alarms & reminders access. Without it, Android may delay timer endings and schedule changes.

For a recurring schedule, tap Start and End to choose exact times, select weekdays and grant Do Not Disturb access if needed. Tap “%4$s” to save changes. “%5$s” stops the recurring schedule. Schedules can cross midnight and use the displayed device time zone.

Android may delay schedule changes while idle. Check the shown Comfer status, Android Do Not Disturb status and next boundary when troubleshooting.
Live notifications and unavailable previews

The main inbox displays current notifications in memory. With “%1$s” enabled, opening an eligible notification saves its copy first. After opening succeeds, Comfer requests dismissal when allowed. A saved copy appears in “%1$s” after the live notification is removed. Optional “%1$s” saves encrypted local text copies of future eligible notifications after consent. Copies remain until retention expiry or deletion and cannot use the original notification action. Choose 24 hours, 7 days or 30 days and exclude apps in “%1$s”. Search finds copies by text, app and date. “%1$s” is limited to 500 copies and is excluded from configuration backups. Locked, secret and protected events are skipped; capture can have gaps. Android may hide sensitive text or provide a limited preview; use Open for the full content. Calls, alarms, media and other protected ongoing notifications may have fewer available actions.
How to open and keep a notification

Enable “%1$s” under “%2$s” → “%1$s” to retain eligible copies. Tap a notification to expand a long preview, then tap again to open its destination. A one-line preview opens immediately. After launch, Comfer requests dismissal. Find the saved copy in “%3$s” after it leaves “%4$s”. Android-redacted, secret and protected content is not saved. If “%1$s” is off, opened notifications are dismissed without creating a copy.
How to silence one app

1. Long press one of the app’s notifications.
2. Tap “%1$s”, then “%2$s”.
3. In Android settings, silence the category or change the app’s allowed notifications. Available controls vary by phone and app.

Use “%3$s” to return to the selected notification.
How to focus now or quiet notifications overnight

For a short break: open “%1$s” → “%2$s” → “%3$s”, grant Do Not Disturb access if prompted, then choose Focus 15, 30 or 60 min. Resume schedules and timers first if it is paused.\n\nFor nights: open “%2$s” → “%4$s” and set a start time such as 22:00 and an end time such as 07:00, choose the start weekdays, then tap “%5$s”. Review Android priority exceptions for the alerts you still want.
How to clear several notifications

1. Long press a notification to select it.
2. Tap other notifications or their selection circles; filled circles mark selected items.
3. If all selected items support dismissal, tap “%1$s”, then “%2$s”.

For one notification, swipe it left or right to dismiss directly. For multiple selections, “%3$s” clears the selection. Deselect the last item or use “%4$s” to exit selection. Protected items cannot be dismissed through Comfer.
How to find missing notifications

First check “%1$s” and the sorting choice in “%2$s”. If access is missing, tap “%3$s” and enable Comfer. If the inbox is reconnecting, use “%4$s”. If it still cannot reconnect, turn Comfer notification access off and on in Android settings.\n\nA healthy empty inbox means there are no current notifications in that view. If “%5$s” was enabled when a notification arrived, its saved copy may still be available in the “%1$s” tab. Enabling “%5$s” cannot recover earlier dismissed notifications.
